questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 MARKS) - QUESTION ONE: DISEASE AND IMMUNITY (10 MARKS)
questions.question: Look at the diagram about ways of transmission of diseases. A. Give one example of a disease that can be transmitted in each of the ways shown above. 1. (1 mark) 2. (1 mark) 3. (1 mark) 4. (1 mark) 5. (1 mark). B. Cholera is a food-borne disease. Write two ways of its prevention. 1. (1 mark) 2. (1 mark). C. There is another way of disease transmission which can be through sexual contact (STDs). i. Name any two disease that can be transmitted in this way. 1. (1 mark) 2. (1 mark). D. Suppose a person got sick and recovered after days. i. Which type of immunity does the person receive? (1 mark).

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 440 270' style='max-width:100%;height:auto' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round'><defs><marker id='a11' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='7' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 Z' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'/></marker></defs><circle cx='45' cy='60' r='18'/><path d='M45 78 V170 M45 100 L15 150 M45 100 L75 150 M45 170 L25 240 M45 170 L65 240'/><circle cx='395' cy='60' r='18'/><path d='M395 78 V170 M395 100 L365 150 M395 100 L425 150 M395 170 L375 240 M395 170 L415 240'/><g marker-end='url(#a11)'><path d='M80 40 H360'/><path d='M80 80 H360'/><path d='M80 120 H360'/><path d='M80 160 H360'/><path d='M80 200 H360'/></g><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none' font-size='13' font-family='sans-serif' text-anchor='middle'><text x='220' y='34'>1. Direct contact</text><text x='220' y='74'>2. Air-borne</text><text x='220' y='114'>3. Food-borne</text><text x='220' y='154'>4. Vector-borne</text><text x='220' y='194'>5. Pet-borne</text><text x='220' y='14' font-style='italic'>Ways of disease transmission from host to another</text></g></svg>
diagram.caption: Diagram titled 'Ways of disease transmission from host to another' showing five numbered routes between two people. The scan is blurred, so the route names are a best reading.

questions.answer_guide: A. 1 Direct contact: scabies / ringworm / skin infections. 2 Air-borne: tuberculosis / influenza / measles. 3 Food-borne (or water-borne): cholera / typhoid. 4 Vector-borne: malaria / dengue (mosquito). 5 Pet or animal-borne: rabies. B. Any two: wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet; drink boiled or treated water; cook food thoroughly and keep it covered; use latrines and dispose of waste properly; vaccination. C. Any two: HIV/AIDS, syphilis, gonorrhoea, chlamydia, hepatitis B. D. Natural active immunity (the body made its own antibodies after catching the disease).

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 MARKS) - QUESTION TWO: SUPPORT AND MOVEMENT (8 MARKS)
questions.question: The diagram shows types of joints and bones. A. Name the parts labeled R, and T. R. (1 mark) T. (1 mark). B. Name the types of joints found in Q and S. Q. (1 mark) S. (1 mark). C. Give any joint other than Q and S you can find in your body. (2 marks). D. Compare and contrast the functions of Q and S. (2 marks).

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 240' style='max-width:100%;height:auto' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'><path d='M120 40 Q160 20 200 40 L190 70 H130 Z'/><circle cx='160' cy='85' r='22'/><path d='M160 107 L175 170'/><circle cx='178' cy='185' r='22'/><path d='M178 207 L150 235'/><path d='M100 140 H150' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M160 15 V30' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M90 85 H138' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M178 207 V235' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none' font-size='14' font-family='sans-serif'><text x='155' y='12'>T</text><text x='70' y='90'>Q</text><text x='80' y='145'>R</text><text x='205' y='190'>S</text></g></svg>
diagram.caption: Leg bones with T (top, at the pelvis), Q (circled hip joint), R (the long thigh bone) and S (circled knee joint), based on the paper's figure. Placement is approximate.

questions.answer_guide: A. R: femur (thigh bone). T: pelvis (hip bone / pelvic girdle). B. Q: ball-and-socket joint. S: hinge joint. C. Any one: pivot joint (neck, between atlas and axis); gliding joint (wrist or ankle); hinge joint at the elbow or fingers; ball-and-socket at the shoulder (only if not repeating Q). D. Similarity: both are synovial joints that allow movement of the leg. Contrast: Q (ball and socket) allows movement in all directions (swing, rotation) and a wide range, while S (hinge) allows movement in one plane only (bending and straightening, like a door hinge).

diagram.caption: A plate with a canjeero (Somali pancake) showing the spiral pattern on its surface.

questions.answer_guide: A. Flour (sorghum / wheat flour), water and yeast (also acceptable: a little sugar and salt). B. Warm temperature is the best for yeast to ferment quickly, producing carbon dioxide bubbles that make the batter rise and form the holes. C. Glucose --yeast--> ethanol (alcohol) + carbon dioxide + energy.

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 MARKS) - QUESTION FOUR: ECOLOGY (16 MARKS)
questions.question: A. This is a food web in a certain ecosystem. i. Name the producer of the food web. (1 mark). ii. Identify the organism with the highest number of predators. (1 mark). iii. From the food web, construct two food chains which end with hawk. (2 marks). B. Name the trophic level occupied by each of the following: i. Mouse (1 mark). ii. Owl (1 mark). iii. Grass (1 mark). iv. Rabbit (1 mark). C. Identify the organism that has the least energy in this food web. (1 mark). D. What would happen to the number of grasshoppers if hawk is killed by a disease? (1 mark). E. Explain the following terms: i. Producers (2 marks). ii. Herbivores (2 marks). iii. Secondary consumers (2 marks).

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 460 340' style='max-width:100%;height:auto' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2'><defs><marker id='a14' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='7' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 Z' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'/></marker></defs><g marker-end='url(#a14)'><path d='M200 300 L68 238'/><path d='M225 300 L205 266'/><path d='M270 300 L385 266'/><path d='M400 235 V168'/><path d='M370 250 L240 250'/><path d='M400 135 L395 78'/><path d='M205 235 L205 150'/><path d='M215 240 L370 78'/><path d='M195 235 L228 42'/><path d='M50 205 L55 78'/><path d='M70 205 L205 38'/><path d='M370 55 L258 30'/><path d='M215 115 L226 42'/></g><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none' font-size='14' font-family='sans-serif' text-anchor='middle'><text x='230' y='22'>Hawk</text><text x='55' y='65'>Fox</text><text x='395' y='65'>Snake</text><text x='205' y='132'>Owl</text><text x='405' y='152'>Bird</text><text x='50' y='222'>Rabbit</text><text x='205' y='256'>Mouse</text><text x='405' y='254'>Grasshopper</text><text x='235' y='325'>Grass</text></g></svg>
diagram.caption: Food web with Grass (producer), Rabbit, Mouse and Grasshopper (primary consumers), Bird, Owl, Fox and Snake, and Hawk at the top. Arrows point to the feeder. The arrow layout is a best reading of a small scan.

questions.answer_guide: A.i. Grass. ii. Mouse (eaten by the owl, snake and hawk; reading depends on the arrows in the figure). iii. Any two: Grass → Mouse → Hawk; Grass → Rabbit → Hawk; Grass → Grasshopper → Bird → Snake → Hawk. B. i. Mouse: second trophic level (primary consumer). ii. Owl: third trophic level (secondary consumer). iii. Grass: first trophic level (producer). iv. Rabbit: second trophic level (primary consumer). C. Hawk (the top consumer, at the end of the chains, receives the least energy). D. The number of grasshoppers would probably increase at first (the snake population grows without the hawk, so fewer birds survive to eat grasshoppers), until limited by food (grass). E. i. Producers: green plants that make their own food by photosynthesis using sunlight, and are the first trophic level. ii. Herbivores: animals that feed only on plants (primary consumers). iii. Secondary consumers: carnivores (or omnivores) that feed on primary consumers; third trophic level.

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 MARKS) - QUESTION FIVE: REPRODUCTION IN HUMANS (11 MARKS)
questions.question: The diagram shows stages in the formation of a humans fetus. A. Name the process of cell division that sperm and egg cells are produced? (1 mark). B. State the number of chromosomes found in each of these. i. Sperm cell (1 mark). ii. Egg cell (1 mark). iii. Fertilized egg cell (1 mark). Fetus (1 mark). C. State the term used to describe the fertilized egg cell. (1 mark). D. Explain what determines 'a fertilized egg cell' to develop into a boy rather than a girl. (2 marks). E. Define these terms: i. Sperm (1 mark). ii. Egg (1 mark). iii. Gametes (1 mark).

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 540 170' style='max-width:100%;height:auto' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round'><defs><marker id='a15' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='7' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0 0 L8 4 L0 8 Z' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'/></marker></defs><ellipse cx='30' cy='40' rx='10' ry='6'/><path d='M40 40 C55 30 60 50 75 40'/><circle cx='50' cy='100' r='14'/><circle cx='50' cy='100' r='3' fill='currentColor'/><path d='M85 70 H125' marker-end='url(#a15)'/><circle cx='150' cy='70' r='16'/><circle cx='150' cy='70' r='4' fill='currentColor'/><path d='M180 70 H220' marker-end='url(#a15)'/><circle cx='265' cy='70' r='38'/><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none'><circle cx='250' cy='58' r='4'/><circle cx='265' cy='52' r='4'/><circle cx='280' cy='58' r='4'/><circle cx='250' cy='74' r='4'/><circle cx='266' cy='70' r='4'/><circle cx='281' cy='76' r='4'/><circle cx='258' cy='88' r='4'/><circle cx='274' cy='90' r='4'/></g><path d='M315 70 H355' marker-end='url(#a15)'/><path d='M375 125 C360 40 400 15 470 25 C510 35 510 100 470 125 Z'/><path d='M410 90 C395 60 420 45 440 60 C455 75 440 100 425 100'/><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none' font-size='12' font-family='sans-serif' text-anchor='middle'><text x='35' y='20'>Sperm cell</text><text x='50' y='132'>Egg cell</text><text x='150' y='105'>Fertilised egg cell</text><text x='265' y='125'>Ball of cells</text><text x='440' y='12'>Amniotic fluid</text><text x='400' y='142'>Amniotic sac</text><text x='430' y='158'>Fetus</text></g></svg>
diagram.caption: Stages in the formation of a human fetus: sperm cell and egg cell fuse to form a fertilised egg cell, which divides into a ball of cells and then develops into a fetus in the amniotic sac with amniotic fluid.

questions.answer_guide: A. Meiosis. B. i. Sperm cell: 23 chromosomes. ii. Egg cell: 23 chromosomes. iii. Fertilized egg cell: 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). Fetus: 46 chromosomes in each body cell. C. Zygote. D. The sex chromosome carried by the sperm. Every egg carries an X; if a sperm carrying a Y fertilizes it the zygote is XY and develops into a boy, whereas an X sperm gives XX (a girl). E. i. Sperm: the male gamete (sex cell), a small haploid cell with a tail made in the testes. ii. Egg: the female gamete (sex cell), a large haploid cell made in the ovaries. iii. Gametes: haploid sex cells (sperm and egg) that fuse at fertilization to form a zygote.

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 MARKS) - QUESTION SIX: GENETICS (18 MARKS)
questions.question: The diagram shows the offspring of a cross between two wolves. Brown colour is caused by dominant allele B and white colour by recessive allele b. A. Write down the phenotype and genotype of wolf R. i. Phenotype (1 mark). ii. Genotype (1 mark). iii. Write down all the genotypes of the offspring 1 to 4. 1. 2. 3. 4. (4 marks). iv. What is the genotypic ratio of the offsprings? (1 mark). B. If the offspring 3 and 4 are crossed again. i. Write down all possible genotypes of the first offsprings. (4 marks). ii. Write down their phenotypic ratio. (1 mark). C. Complete the following sentences using genetic terms from the box (6 marks). Box: Phenotype, complete dominance, Homozygous, heterozygous, chromosome and gene. 1. ............ is the out-word appearance of an organism. 2. ............ is thread-like structure composed of DNA and genes found in the nucleus. 3. ............ is a section of DNA molecule. 4. ............ having two different alleles for a particular gene locus. 5. ............ having same alleles for a particular gene locus. 6. ............ is when an allele of a gene completely masks the allele of another gene.

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 420 220' style='max-width:100%;height:auto' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round'><path d='M210 60 V110 M60 110 H360 M60 110 V140 M150 110 V140 M250 110 V140 M350 110 V140'/><ellipse cx='90' cy='40' rx='40' ry='16' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='.35'/><path d='M60 54 l-6 20 M120 54 l6 20'/><ellipse cx='60' cy='165' rx='30' ry='14'/><ellipse cx='150' cy='165' rx='30' ry='14'/><ellipse cx='250' cy='165' rx='30' ry='14'/><ellipse cx='350' cy='165' rx='30' ry='14'/><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none' font-size='14' font-family='sans-serif' text-anchor='middle'><text x='90' y='45'>Bb</text><text x='160' y='45'>×</text><text x='225' y='45'>Wolf R</text><text x='60' y='205'>1</text><text x='150' y='205'>2</text><text x='250' y='205'>3</text><text x='350' y='205'>4</text></g></svg>
diagram.caption: A brown wolf of genotype Bb is crossed with Wolf R and produces four offspring numbered 1 to 4. The paper's drawing shows the wolves as silhouettes; this is a schematic redraw.

questions.answer_guide: A. The paper does not state wolf R's colour in text; the answer below assumes R is brown and heterozygous. i. Phenotype: brown. ii. Genotype: Bb. iii. Cross Bb × Bb gives offspring genotypes BB, Bb, Bb and bb, for example 1 = BB, 2 = Bb, 3 = Bb, 4 = bb (offspring 4 is the white wolf in the picture). iv. Genotypic ratio 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb. B. i. Crossing offspring 3 (Bb) with offspring 4 (bb) gives Bb, Bb, bb, bb (genotypes Bb and bb). ii. Phenotypic ratio: 1 brown : 1 white (2 brown : 2 white). C. 1 Phenotype; 2 Chromosome; 3 Gene; 4 Heterozygous; 5 Homozygous; 6 Complete dominance.

questions.section: PART TWO: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (90 MARKS) - QUESTION SEVEN: NERVOUS SYSTEM (6 MARKS)
questions.question: This is a diagram of nerve cell. A. State the type of nerve cell. (1 mark). B. State one main feature that distinguish it from other types of nerve cells. (1 mark). C. Name the parts labeled 1 and 3. (1 mark). D. State the function of part labeled 3. (1 mark). E. Use a line and number to label these two parts on the diagram: nucleus and cytoplasm. (2 marks).

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 520 280' style='max-width:100%;height:auto' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round'><circle cx='150' cy='130' r='115' stroke-opacity='.6'/><path d='M110 120 C90 100 70 100 60 85 M110 120 C80 125 60 130 50 125 M115 140 C95 160 80 175 70 195 M130 155 C130 180 125 200 115 215 M150 105 C150 80 160 65 170 50 M170 110 C190 90 205 80 215 70'/><ellipse cx='150' cy='130' rx='45' ry='38' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='.2'/><circle cx='150' cy='130' r='12' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='.5'/><path d='M195 130 H410'/><g fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='.25'><rect x='230' y='122' width='40' height='16' rx='8'/><rect x='280' y='122' width='40' height='16' rx='8'/><rect x='330' y='122' width='40' height='16' rx='8'/></g><path d='M410 130 L450 100 M410 130 L455 130 M410 130 L450 160 M450 100 L470 90 M450 160 L470 170'/><path d='M215 70 L232 50' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M180 235 L200 255' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M300 70 V120' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M390 195 H455' stroke-width='1.5'/><g fill='currentColor' stroke='none' font-size='14' font-family='sans-serif'><text x='235' y='48'>1.</text><text x='203' y='268'>2.</text><text x='296' y='62'>3.</text><text x='380' y='200'>4.</text></g></svg>
diagram.caption: A nerve cell (neuron) inside a circle, with a cell body, short branching processes on the left, a long fibre with sheath segments, and branched endings on the right. Parts are labelled 1 to 4.

questions.answer_guide: A. Motor neuron. B. It has a long axon and short dendrites, with its cell body at one end (the cell body is not off to the side as in a sensory neuron). C. 1: dendrite (dendrites receiving impulses). 3: axon (nerve fibre, with its myelin sheath). D. The axon carries nerve impulses away from the cell body towards other neurons, muscles or glands (the myelin sheath insulates it and speeds up impulses). E. Label the nucleus as the dark central round structure inside the cell body, and the cytoplasm as the yellow area around the nucleus within the cell body. Note: the figure is small and unclear, so which part each number points to should be checked against the original.

questions.answer_guide: A.i. Eye, nose, tongue and skin. ii. Nose (smell) and tongue (taste). iii. 1: pinna (outer ear flap). 2: ear canal (auditory canal) leading to the eardrum. 3: Eustachian tube. 4: cochlea. (Which part each number points to should be checked against the original figure.) iv. 1 (the pinna). v. Outer ear, middle ear and inner ear. vi. Ear wax (cerumen), which traps dust and microbes. B.i. Their large, movable outer ears (pinnae) collect more sound and can be turned to the sound, and they need very good hearing to detect predators or prey and to communicate; their ears can detect a wider range of frequencies (higher-pitched sounds) than humans.
